title: Lesson 12: Focused Read-aloud and Retelling, Session 1: Why the Sun and the Moon Live in the Sky
objective: Students will answer questions about key details and describe characters, setting, and major events from the story Why the Sun and the Moon Live in the Sky, using oral discussion, role-play, and independent writing.

what_is_taught.skill: answer questions about key details from a story
describe major events from a story
use a signal to identify story elements during read-aloud
turn and talk with a partner to discuss story details
participate in role-play to retell story elements
use puppets to represent characters during role-play
write responses about characters and setting using a response sheet
use classroom resources to support writing
engage in partner and whole group discussion to reflect on learning
use sentence frames and language supports to explain story details
identify and discuss vocabulary related to story elements
demonstrate respect and care for classroom materials and environment

student_actions.recognition_identification: identify story elements and vocabulary words during read-aloud and word wall review
student_actions.oral_production: answer questions, share ideas in partner and whole group discussions, participate in role-play, and reflect orally on learning
student_actions.written_production: write responses about characters and setting on a response sheet
student_actions.matching_sorting_sequencing: sequence story events during role-play and place story element icons on the board
student_actions.procedural_application: use protocols for role-play and partner discussions
student_actions.investigation_handson: engage physically by moving bodies to represent characters and care for puppets
student_actions.representation_modeling: use puppets to represent characters and demonstrate respectful behavior
student_actions.reasoning_explanation: explain story details and reasons for characters' actions orally and in writing
student_actions.comprehension_response: respond to questions about key details and story elements orally and in writing, including retelling and summarizing story parts and reflecting on learning progress in discussions and partner talk, using sentence frames and language supports as needed, including for ELLs and students needing scaffolding, and participate in a mini language dive to understand sentence chunks in the story text, supported by sketches and word banks for vocabulary and meaning

evidence.quote: Display the 'Sun, Moon, and Stars' song and invite students to sing and move along with you as you sing the complete song in the present tense.
If time permits, repeat the song in the past tense and in the future tense.
I can answer questions about key details from Why the Sun and the Moon Live in the Sky.

Display Why the Sun and the Moon Live in the Sky and remind students that, as in previous lessons, they will use a signal to show when they see or hear a character introduced in the story. Demonstrate the signal (thumbs-up, pat your head, touch your toes, etc.).
Draw students' attention back to the book and read aloud pages 1-12 slowly, fluently, with expression, and without interruption, looking for students to use the designated signal.
'Who are the characters?' (Sun, Moon, and Water)
Why the Sun and the Moon
'As you look carefully at the illustration, what details help you understand the setting?' (huts or houses made of grass, a pathway, people in costumes, etc.)
'Based on these details, when and where is this story taking place?' (a long time ago in a village or small town on earth)
Invite a student volunteer to come up and place the Story Elements board icon for village on the board.
Briefly review the words: sun, moon, sky, and earth.
'What has Water done so far in the story? How is that affecting Sun and Moon?' (Water brought friends to the house and they are filling up the house, so Sun and Moon have no space.)

Draw students' attention back to the text and read the remainder of it. Invite students to move their bodies to pretend to be the Moon or the Sun going up in the sky as the read-aloud comes to a close.
'At the end of the story, why did Sun and Moon go up into the sky?' (because their house was overflowed with water and there was no room for them)
'Who can tell us what your classmate said in your own words?' (Responses will vary.)
Invite students to turn and talk with an elbow partner:
Why the Sun and the Moon
Why the Sun and the Moon

Give students specific, positive feedback on their ability to show care for their environment. (Example: 'Angela and Eliot showed how to be effective learners with respect to their environment when Eliot dropped his sun puppet and Angela very carefully picked it up and handed it to him.')
Why the Sun and the Moon
Why the Sun and the Moon

Circulate to support students as they write. Encourage them to use classroom resources (Story Elements board, Word Walls, high-frequency word lists, and alphabet or letter sound combination charts). If students need additional support generating ideas, invite them to work in a small group with support and refer to the Story Elements board from Work Time A.
Invite students to move back into a circle around the whole group meeting area.
Guide students through the protocol using the following question:
Invite students to return to their seats and engage in a whole group discussion regarding their responses as time permits.

teacher_actions.direct_instruction: Model reading the story aloud with expression and fluency; demonstrate the use of signals to identify story elements; model the use of sentence frames and language chunks for ELLs; model respectful care for classroom materials; model the role-play protocol.
prompts_that_cue_student_response: As you look carefully at the illustration, what details help you understand the setting?
Based on these details, when and where is this story taking place?
What has Water done so far in the story? How is that affecting Sun and Moon?
At the end of the story, why did Sun and Moon go up into the sky?
Who can tell us what your classmate said in your own words?
How can we work to become effective learners and care for the puppets?
How did you work to become and effective learner for yourself, your classmates, and the classroom environment during today's lesson?
